s0401.literal: On the road he met bandits; Zhuo was haggard and wretched, wailing and pleading his case; the bandits pitied him and did not kill him, but still escorted him out of the territory.
s0401.idiomatic: On the road he met bandits. Zhuo was wasted and wretched, wailing and pleading his case; the bandits pitied him and did not kill him, but escorted him out of the territory.

s0402.literal: When he crossed Pengli Lake, midstream he suddenly met a violent wind; the boat nearly sank four times; Zhuo lamented to Heaven, and shortly the wind ceased—people all took it as the utmost reach of filial feeling moving Heaven.
s0402.idiomatic: Crossing Pengli Lake, he met a sudden gale midstream and the boat nearly sank four times. Zhuo cried out to Heaven; the wind soon ceased, and all took it as filial feeling moving Heaven to the utmost.

s0403.literal: When Shuling was executed, Houzhu said to the court ministers: "Ruan Zhuo from of old was not one with the rebels; he should receive special honor and distinction.
s0403.idiomatic: When Shuling was executed, Houzhu told the court, "Ruan Zhuo was never of the rebels; he should be specially honored."

s0404.literal: " In Zhide year 1 he entered service as academician of the Hall of Virtue and Instruction.
s0404.idiomatic: In Zhide year 1 he entered as academician of the Hall of Virtue and Instruction.

s0405.literal: Soon he was also made direct-and-plain attendant of the scattered cavalry, deputy to Wang Hua on the mission to Sui.
s0405.idiomatic: Soon he was also direct-and-plain attendant of the scattered cavalry, deputy to Wang Hua on the mission to Sui.

s0406.literal: The Sui Emperor had long heard Zhuo's name and therefore sent Xue Daoheng of Hedong, Yan Zhitui of Langye, and others to feast and compose poetry with Zhuo, with gifts and courtesy added.
s0406.idiomatic: The Sui Emperor had long heard of Zhuo and sent Xue Daoheng of Hedong, Yan Zhitui of Langye, and others to feast and compose poetry with him, with added gifts and courtesy.

s0407.literal: On return he was made General Who Draws Distant and staff adviser to the Prince of Nanhai's household.
s0407.idiomatic: On return he was made general who draws distant and staff adviser to the prince of Nanhai's household.

s0408.literal: Eye disease kept him from taking office; he retired to his village dwelling, rebuilt pavilions, repaired hill ponds and ornamental plants, gathered guests, and took literature and wine for his pleasure.
s0408.idiomatic: Eye disease kept him from office; he retired home, rebuilt pavilions, laid out ponds and gardens, gathered guests, and amused himself with books and wine.

s0409.literal: In Zhenming year 3 he entered Sui; reaching Jiangzhou, moved by the place where his father had ended, he fell ill and died, aged fifty-nine.
s0409.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered Sui; at Jiangzhou, moved by where his father had died, he fell ill and died at fifty-nine.

s0410.literal: At the time there was Yin Keng of Wuwei, styled Zijian, son of Liang's Left Guard General Zichun.
s0410.idiomatic: At the time Yin Keng of Wuwei, styled Zijian, was son of Liang's left guard general Zichun.

s0411.literal: From youth he was clever; at five he could recite poetry and rhapsodies, a thousand characters a day.
s0411.idiomatic: Clever from youth, at five he could recite poetry and rhapsodies—a thousand characters a day.

s0412.literal: When grown he was broadly versed in histories and records, especially skilled in five-character poetry, and was highly regarded in his time.
s0412.idiomatic: Grown, he was broadly versed in histories and especially skilled in five-character poetry, highly regarded in his day.

s0413.literal: On first appointment he was law-bureau officer in the Prince of Xiangdong's Liang kingdom.
s0413.idiomatic: On first appointment he was law-bureau officer in the prince of Xiangdong's Liang kingdom.

s0414.literal: In cold weather Keng once feasted with guests and drinking companions; seeing the wine-server pass by, he turned back roast meat and gave it to him; the whole company laughed. Keng said: "We spend the whole day in deep drinking, yet the cup-bearer does not know the taste—not human feeling.
s0414.idiomatic: One cold day Keng feasted with guests; seeing the wine-server pass, he sent back roast meat for him. The company laughed. Keng said, "We drink all day, yet the cup-bearer never tastes the wine—not human feeling."

s0415.literal: " When Hou Jing's rebellion came, Keng was once seized by bandits; someone rescued him and he was spared. Keng asked the reason—it was the wine-server of before.
s0415.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion Keng was once seized by bandits; someone rescued him. He asked why—it was the wine-server from before.

s0416.literal: In Tianchen he was recorder in the Prince of Shixing's household.
s0416.idiomatic: In Tianchen he was recorder in the prince of Shixing's household.

s0417.literal: Emperor Wen once banqueted the ministers and ordered them to compose poetry; Xu Ling spoke of him to Emperor Wen, and that same day Keng was summoned to the banquet and ordered to compose on the newly completed Ancheng Palace of Peace and Joy; Keng took brush and finished at once—Emperor Wen greatly admired him.
s0417.idiomatic: Emperor Wen once banqueted the ministers for poetry; Xu Ling spoke of Keng to him, and that day Keng was summoned and told to compose on the new Ancheng Palace of Peace and Joy. He wrote at once, and Emperor Wen greatly admired him.

s0418.literal: He was repeatedly advanced to General Who Draws Distant, administrator of Jinling, and supernumerary irregular attendant of the scattered cavalry; shortly he died.
s0418.idiomatic: He rose to general who draws distant, Jinling administrator, and supernumerary irregular attendant of the scattered cavalry; soon he died.

s0419.literal: He had a collection of three scrolls in circulation in the world.
s0419.idiomatic: A collection of three scrolls circulated in his time.

s0421.literal: The historiographer says: Literature—is it not the foundation of human relations?
s0421.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Literature—is it not the foundation of human relations?

s0422.literal: Thus the gentleman differs from the common multitude.
s0422.idiomatic: Thus the gentleman differs from the common multitude.

s0423.literal: Formerly, in Confucius's discussion of the four categories, he began with virtue and ended with literature—this too the sage valued.
s0423.idiomatic: Formerly Confucius ranked four categories, beginning with virtue and ending with literature—the sage valued that too.

s0424.literal: As for men like Du Zhiwei, they met a fortunate age and each displayed his talents; Zhiwei was especially distinguished in beauty.
s0424.idiomatic: Men like Du Zhiwei met a fortunate age and each showed his talent; Zhiwei was especially distinguished.

s0425.literal: "Jiang Dezao styled Dezao"—or in some texts "Jiang Dezao styled Dezao"—is doubtful.
s0425.idiomatic: Whether the name reads Jiang Dezao (cao) styled Dezao or Jiang Dezao (zao) styled Dezao is doubtful.

s0429.literal: [Tong] year 1 Liang Emperor Wu at Tongtai Temple renounced the body and ordered Xu Mian to draft and fix the ritual regulations
s0429.idiomatic: On "[Tong] year 1 Liang Emperor Wu at Tongtai Temple renounced the body and ordered Xu Mian to draft and fix the ritual regulations"

s0430.literal: Note: checking the Annals of Emperor Wu in the Book of Liang, Liang Emperor Wu in the ninth month of Zhongdatong year 1 went to Tongtai Temple and renounced the body—clearly "Central Great Unity" is an error for "Central Grand Passage"; now emended accordingly.
s0430.idiomatic: The Book of Liang, Annals of Emperor Wu, has Liang Wudi renounce the body at Tongtai in the ninth month of Zhongdatong year 1; Central Great Unity is an error for Central Grand Passage and is now emended.

s0431.literal: [2] "made Zhiwei manage the secretariat"—the character "wei" was originally missing in the base text; supplied according to all editions.
s0431.idiomatic: On "[2] made Zhiwei manage the secretariat": wei was missing in the base text and is supplied per all editions.

s0434.literal: [cheng] duke's study"—changed according to the Biography of the Prince of Southern Commandery, Dalian, in the Book of Liang.
s0434.idiomatic: On "[cheng] duke's study": emended per the biography of Prince of Southern Commandery Dalian in the Book of Liang.

s0435.literal: Note: in Sun Wu's Chiwu era, territory of Lingyang and Shicheng counties was split off to establish Lincheng county; under Liang it belonged to Nanling commandery.
s0435.idiomatic: In Sun Wu's Chiwu era, parts of Lingyang and Shicheng were split off as Lincheng county; under Liang it belonged to Nanling commandery.

s0436.literal: [4] "[Datong] seventh year"—supplied according to the Southern History.
s0436.idiomatic: On "[4] [Datong] seventh year": supplied per the Southern History.

s0437.literal: [5] "at the time the Music Bureau lacked lyrics for Confucius and Yanzi ascending"—"ge" in all editions is written "song."
s0437.idiomatic: On "[5] at the time the Music Bureau lacked lyrics for Confucius and Yanzi ascending": ge in all editions is written song.

s0438.literal: Note: ge is the ancient form of the character for song.
s0438.idiomatic: Ge is the ancient form of the character for song.

s0439.literal: [6] "your servant has no room hastily to change market and court"—"change" in Yuan Gui 464 reads "cherish."
s0439.idiomatic: On "[6] your servant has no room hastily to change market and court": change in Yuan Gui 464 reads cherish.

s0442.literal: [zao] styled Dezao"—changed according to the Northern Supervisory, Hall, and Southern History editions.
s0442.idiomatic: On "[zao] styled Dezao": emended per the Northern Supervisory, Hall, and Southern History editions.

s0443.literal: Note: this book's general table of contents and sectional tables all read "Dezao," and the later text of this biography is the same; Hong Yijun's Collation of Various Histories and Zhang Senkai's collation notes alike treat writing "Dezao" as the error.
s0443.idiomatic: This book's tables and this biography later read Dezao; Hong Yijun and Zhang Senkai both treat writing Dezao (cao) as the error.

s0444.literal: [8] "from Tianchen year 4 to together with Secretariat attendant Liu Shizhi on a mission to Qi"—according to the Biography of the Prince of Nan'ang, the Deposed, Tanlang, Jiang Dezao and Liu Shizhi went on a mission to Qi to escort Tanlang's coffin and returned to the capital in the spring of Tianchen year 3; therefore Dezao's mission to Qi should have been before year 3—"year 4" is probably an error for "year 2."
s0444.idiomatic: On "[8] from Tianchen year 4 with Secretariat attendant Liu Shizhi on a mission to Qi": per the biography of Prince Nan'ang Tanlang, Dezao and Shizhi escorted the coffin from Qi and returned in spring of Tianchen year 3; the mission must have been before year 3—year 4 is probably year 2.

s0445.literal: [9] "Yu Chi styled Yunde"—"Yunde" in the Southern History reads "Yuande."
s0445.idiomatic: On "[9] Yu Chi styled Yunde": Yunde in the Southern History reads Yuande.

s0446.literal: [10] "father [Sha]mi"—supplied according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.
s0446.idiomatic: On "[10] father [Sha]mi": supplied per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.

s0447.literal: Note: Yu Shami has a biography in the Book of Liang.
s0447.idiomatic: Yu Shami has a biography in the Book of Liang.

s0448.literal: [11] "early in Tianjian the Founder and Chi had old ties"—Zhang Senkai's collation note says: "The Founder was born in Tianjian year 2—how could the Founder at the beginning of Tianjian already have old ties with Chi?
s0448.idiomatic: On "[11] early in Tianjian the Founder and Chi had old ties": Zhang Senkai's note says the Founder was born in Tianjian year 2—how could he already have old ties with Chi at the start of Tianjian?

s0449.literal: This must certainly be an error."
s0449.idiomatic: This must certainly be an error."

s0450.literal: On further examination: judging by the sequence of events in the biography, "Tianjian" is probably an error for "Taiqing."
s0450.idiomatic: On further examination, judging by the sequence of events in the biography, Tianjian is probably an error for Taiqing.

s0451.literal: [12] "punished for beating a county man to death and lost enfeoffment"—the Southern History lacks the character "enfeoffment."
s0451.idiomatic: On "[12] punished for beating a county man to death and lost enfeoffment": the Southern History lacks enfeoffment.

s0452.literal: Note: above it says "Emperor Wen was angry with him and therefore punished him by dismissal"—that was removal from Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; only here is his enfeoffment finally taken away—the character "enfeoffment" is not a spurious addition.
s0452.idiomatic: Above, Emperor Wen's anger led to dismissal from left vice director; only here is enfeoffment finally lost—enfeoffment is not redundant.

s0455.literal: [return] made Gentlemen Attendant of the Yellow Gate—changed according to the Southern History.
s0455.idiomatic: On "[return] made Gentlemen Attendant of the Yellow Gate": emended per the Southern History.

s0456.literal: Note: this refers to after Chi was removed as magistrate of Lin'an and returned to the capital as Gentlemen Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
s0456.idiomatic: After Chi left the Lin'an magistracy he returned to the capital as Gentlemen Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

s0457.literal: "Transfer" and "return" are graphically similar and were corrupted.
s0457.idiomatic: Transfer and return are graphically similar and were corrupted.

s0458.literal: [14] "on first appointment, staff officer in the Prince of Andong's Liang kingdom"—Zhang Senkai's collation note says: "Liang had no Prince of Andong; Andong is a general's title—probably there is lacuna after the character 'east.'"
s0458.idiomatic: On "[14] on first appointment, staff officer in the Prince of Andong's Liang kingdom": Zhang Senkai notes Liang had no prince of Andong; Andong is a general's title—probably text is missing after east.

s0459.literal: [15] "the authorities collected Sengbian and his son Yan's [corpse]"—"corpse" supplied according to the Northern Supervisory, Hall editions, and Southern History.
s0459.idiomatic: On "[15] the authorities collected Sengbian and his son Yan's [corpse]": corpse supplied per the Northern Supervisory, Hall editions, and Southern History.

s0460.literal: [16] "together used family wealth to arrange the funeral
s0460.idiomatic: On "[16] together used family wealth to arrange the funeral"

s0462.literal: "—deleted according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, Hall editions, and Southern History.
s0462.idiomatic: implements—deleted per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, Hall editions, and Southern History.

s0463.literal: [17] "encountered a fierce beast"—"beast" in the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions reads "tiger," the same below.
s0463.idiomatic: On "[17] encountered a fierce beast": beast in the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions reads tiger, the same below.

s0464.literal: Note: the Southern History also reads "beast"—probably to avoid Tang taboo.
s0464.idiomatic: The Southern History also reads beast—probably Tang taboo avoidance.

s0465.literal: The reading "tiger" is a later restoration.

s0466.literal: [18] "transferred to chief administrator of the Prince of Ancheng"—"administrator" in the base text was wrongly written "son"; other editions are not wrong; now corrected.
s0466.idiomatic: On "[18] transferred to chief administrator of the Prince of Ancheng": administrator in the base text was wrongly written son; other editions are correct; now emended.

s0467.literal: [19] "together personally drafted a sacrificial text and sent an envoy to perform mourning sacrifice"—the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions lack the character "sacrifice" before "text," and lack "envoy" after "sent."
s0467.idiomatic: On "[19] together personally drafted a sacrificial text and sent an envoy to perform mourning sacrifice": the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions lack sacrifice before text and envoy after sent.

s0468.literal: [20] "always had sour resentment"—"resentment" in the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions reads "lump in the throat."
s0468.idiomatic: On "[20] always had sour resentment": resentment in the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions reads lump in the throat.

s0469.literal: [21] "Liang Grand Master of Works Yan [zi]'s son"—"zi" supplied according to the Southern History.
s0469.idiomatic: On "[21] Liang Grand Master of Works Yan [zi]'s son": zi supplied per the Southern History.

s0470.literal: Note: in the Biography of Lu Yungong in the Book of Liang, Yungong had an elder brother named Yanzi—this is that Yanzi.
s0470.idiomatic: The Book of Liang biography of Lu Yungong names an elder brother Yanzi—this Yanzi.

s0471.literal: [22] "the Prince of Wuling, as Grand Marshal assuming the regency, appointed him to South Liang province
s0471.idiomatic: On "[22] the Prince of Wuling, as Grand Marshal assuming the regency, appointed him to South Liang province"

s0473.idiomatic: On "[inspector]": emended per the Southern History.

s0474.literal: Note: a province has no "chief administrator."
s0474.idiomatic: A province has no chief administrator.

s0475.literal: [23] "Zhiyuan followed Shaoling prefect Liu Gong to the commandery"—"Liu Gong" in the Southern History reads "Liu Fei."
s0475.idiomatic: On "[23] Zhiyuan followed Shaoling prefect Liu Gong to the commandery": Liu Gong in the Southern History reads Liu Fei.

s0476.literal: The Comprehensive Mirror for Liang Emperor Jing, Shaotai year 1, also has "Shaoling prefect Liu Fei leading troops to relieve Jiangling"—again "Liu Fei."
s0476.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Mirror, Liang Emperor Jing Shaotai year 1, also has Shaoling prefect Liu Fei leading troops to relieve Jiangling.

s0478.literal: [24] "annalistic composition"—"annal" in the base text was wrongly written "continue"; other editions are not wrong; now corrected.
s0478.idiomatic: On "[24] annalistic composition": annal in the base text was wrongly written continue; other editions are correct; now emended.

s0479.literal: [25] "greatly received fine appreciation"—"fine" in the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions reads "commendation."
s0479.idiomatic: On "[25] greatly received fine appreciation": fine in the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions reads commendation.
